sense: all the way to a point

terms.gloss: as far as, all the way to; until
terms.grammar: ad with the accusative, strengthened by the adverb ūsque
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Com. 20: ab īmīs unguibus ūsque ad verticem summum
terms.comment: All the way to a point in space or time: ūsque ad mare, as far as the sea; ā … ūsque ad, from … to. With names of towns, ūsque with the accusative alone is classical (ūsque Rōmam; Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: preposition placed after its noun, with the ablative (in verse and Livy also a genitive plural)
terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov.; also Liv. and post-Augustan prose
terms.comment: Mostly in verse and post-Augustan prose, not in Caesar (Lewis & Short): pectoribus tenus, up to the chest. Verbīs tenus, as far as words go.

phrases.latin: nōn ab īmīs unguibus ūsque ad verticem summum … ex fraude, fallāciīs, mendāciīs cōnstāre tōtus vidētur?
phrases.english: does he not seem, from the tips of his toes to the top of his head, to be made entirely of fraud, tricks and lies?

phrases.latin: dehinc quīntus Quīntīlis et sīc deinceps ūsque ad Decembrem ā numerō
phrases.english: then the fifth, Quintilis, and so on in order as far as December, named from their numbers

phrases.latin: et erat pectoribus tenus aucta nocturnō imbrī
phrases.english: and it had risen with the night’s rain as far as their chests
far from it in deeds, as far as words go
